claim.claim-text: 1. A method for verifying when a user, based on images of the user, does not exhibit three-dimensionality, the method comprising:
2. The method of claim 1, wherein the expected differences result from at least fish-eye distortion.
3. The method of claims 1 or 2, further comprising:

4. The method of any one of claims 1 to 3, further comprising: displaying one or more prompts on a screen associated with the computing device to guide the user to capture the at least one first image at the first distance and the at least one second image at the second distance.

5. The method of claim 4, wherein the one or more prompts are an oval shape within which an image of a face of the user is aligned during capture the at least one first image and the at least one second image.

6. The method of any one of claims 1 to 5, wherein the computing device is a hand-held device, and the user holds the computing device at the first distance from the user when capturing at least one first image and holds the computing device at the second distance from the user when capturing the at least one second image.

7. The method of any one of claims 1 to 6, further comprising: illuminating a screen of the computing device while capturing the at least one first image and/or the at least one second image to improve quality of an image being captured.

8. The method of any one of claims 1 to 7, wherein a face of the user is held steady when capturing the at least one first image and the at least one second image and the camera moves from the first location to the second location.

9. A system for verifying three-dimensionality of a user's face using images of the user's face captured using a camera, the system comprising: a computing device having a processor, a transmit and receive module, and memory configured with non-transitory machine readable code that is executable by the processor, the machine readable code configured to:

10. The system of claim 9, wherein the computing device is configured to display one or more prompts on a screen of the computing device to guide the user to capture the at least one first image at the first distance and the at least on second image at the second distance.

11. The system of claims 9 or 10, wherein the computing device is a server that is remote from a camera equipped computing device that captures the at least one first image and the at least one second image.

12. The system of claims 9 to 11, wherein the camera equipped computing device is a user's hand held computing device, and the user holds the hand held computing device at the first distance when capturing the at least one first image and at the second distance when capturing the at least one second image.

13. A non-transient computer readable medium containing non-transitory machine executable code configured to verify if, based on captured images of a person's face, the captured images of the person's face do not exhibit three-dimensionality, the non-transitory machine executable code configured to:

14. The non-transient computer readable medium of claim 13, wherein the expected differences appear as changes in the relative dimensions of facial features of the person's face captured in the at least one first image or the at least one second image.

15. The non-transient computer readable medium of claim 13 or 14, wherein the expected differences result from fish-eye type distortion in at least one of the at least one first image and the at least one second image that is created due to the three-dimensional nature of the human face and the change in distance between the camera and the person's face when capturing the at least one first image and the at least one second image.
16. The non-transient computer readable medium of claims 13 to 15, wherein the first biometric data and the second biometric data comprise data representing facial features.
